## Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Assignment

In 2–4 sentences, state what the ANOVA tells you in context, note whether the model's assumptions appear reasonable for this data, and say whether the difference you found is large enough to matter practically — not only statistically.

### Perform a one-way ANOVA analysis on the following dataset

```{r}
greenhouse_df <- tibble(
  Control = c(21, 19.5, 22.5, 21.5, 20.5, 21),
  F1 = c(32, 30.5, 25, 27.5, 28, 28.6),
  F2 = c(22.5, 26, 28, 27, 26.5, 25.2),
  F3 = c(28, 27.5, 31, 29.5, 30, 29.2)
)

greenhouse_df
```

#### In order to run the ANOVA test, we need to place the column names into a single column as our "factor"

```{r}
greenhouse_long_df <- greenhouse_df |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "factor", values_to = "measurement")

greenhouse_long_df
```

#### ANOVA using `aov()`

```{r}
greenhouse_aov <- aov(measurement ~ factor, data = greenhouse_long_df)

summary(greenhouse_aov)
```

#### Plot of the data

```{r}
greenhouse_long_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor, y = measurement)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.1))
```

```{r}
TukeyHSD(greenhouse_aov)
```
